lesson_title: Summarising Data with Mean, Median, Mode and Range
hook_text: Three goals a game? Or one? Both are true.
clip_script:
An under-fourteen soccer team plays ten matches and the striker claims the team averages three goals a game. The goalkeeper disagrees: most games they score one. The coach writes the goals on the board, in order of the matches: 1, 0, 2, 1, 1, 3, 1, 0, 1, 20. The twenty was against a side that arrived with eight players.

Order them: 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 20. Total 30, ten matches, mean 3. The striker is right. Median: the fifth and sixth values, both 1. Mode: 1. The goalkeeper is right about a typical match. One freak game made the mean; the median never noticed it. When someone quotes an average, ask which one.
visual_style: A chalkboard of ten match scores; the 20 glows and drags a balance beam labelled MEAN upward while a marker labelled MEDIAN stays put on the 1
call_to_action: Open the full session to calculate every measure and choose the one that tells the truth.
